prompt.context: Your client is a bank in Argentina who has historically served individuals or large corporations. There are only three other large banks in the market, with each having equal market share and cost structures. Last year, your client was the first bank to enter the small to medium business market and made some money. They did this primarily by offering the businesses the same services that they offered the small and large companies through their retail outlets.
prompt.question: They would like to understand how they could become more profitable. How would you approach this?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current profit margin and revenue breakdown?
clarifying_info.a: Current structure: $160M profit, $160M fixed cost, $480M variable cost, $800M total revenue. Revenue per product is $1,000. The client services 2 products per customer.

clarifying_info.q: How price-sensitive are the small and medium business customers?
clarifying_info.a: Users are very price sensitive, so price cannot be easily changed.

clarifying_info.q: How does the client's cost structure compare to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: The cost structure is currently very good (20% profit, 20% fixed, 60% variable).

clarifying_info.q: Is the small to medium business market growing?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the small to medium business market is growing.

clarifying_info.q: Can we acquire new customers or expand to existing ones?
clarifying_info.a: Both options are available: increase sales to current clients or increase sales to new clients.

framework: Analyze the profit equation: Revenue = Price x Quantity; Price cannot easily be changed due to customer price sensitivity; Cost structure is already lean; Therefore focus on increasing Quantity
Two levers for growing quantity: (1) Increase sales to current clients — sell more products per existing customer; (2) Increase sales to new clients — acquire more customers in the SMB market
Identify new products/services to offer SMB customers to drive both levers
Segment the SMB customer base to prioritize and target effectively
Assess financial impact of the growth scenario

questions.prompt: Please give me four examples of products that you would offer to the small and medium sized businesses.
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm banking/financial products relevant to SMB needs. Strong answers include: payroll management, funds management services, tax services, business insurance. Any well-reasoned product with a brief rationale is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Given the new service offerings, we predict customers will increase to 600,000, each taking 3 products per customer. Revenue per product and variable cost per product stay the same. What is the expected profit?
questions.guidance: Candidate must work from current financials to derive variable cost per product, then apply new volume assumptions. Key steps: derive current number of products and variable cost per product, then compute new revenue, fixed cost, variable cost, and profit.

math.setup: Current: $800M revenue / $1,000 revenue per product = 800,000 products. Variable cost per product = $480M / 800,000 = $600 per product. New scenario: 600,000 customers x 3 products = 1,800,000 products.
steps: New Revenue = 600,000 customers x 3 products/customer x $1,000/product = $1,800M
New Variable Costs = 600,000 customers x 3 products/customer x $600/product = $1,080M

questions.prompt: Can you provide a couple of ways to segment our small and medium sized business customers?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose segmentation schemes backed by rationale. Strong answers include: risk susceptibility, size by revenues, size by number of employees, industry type (service vs. production), lender services needs, borrower services needs.

questions.prompt: So, should we move forward with this expansion into the SMB market?
questions.guidance: Candidate should give a clear recommendation, structured with supporting rationale. Given the potential profit jump from $160M to $560M and alignment with current offerings/infrastructure, the benefits far outweigh the risks. Candidate should call it a go and briefly note risks and next steps.

brainstorming.prompt: Can you provide a couple of ways to segment our small and medium sized business customers?

categories.name: Risk-based
ideas: Risk susceptibility — high vs. low credit risk

categories.name: Industry-based
ideas: Industry type: service businesses vs. production/manufacturing businesses

recommendation: Yes, the client should move forward with expanding and deepening its presence in the SMB market
The profit potential is substantial — projected profit grows from $160M to $560M under the new volume scenario — and the expansion leverages existing retail infrastructure and service offerings
risks: Price sensitivity among SMB customers limits ability to raise revenue per product
Competitors may respond by entering the SMB segment, eroding first-mover advantage
Execution risk in delivering new products (payroll, tax, insurance) at scale and quality
next_steps: Segment the SMB customer base (by size, industry, risk profile) to prioritize acquisition and cross-sell efforts
Develop and pilot the additional product offerings (payroll management, funds management, tax services, business insurance)
Set targets for customer acquisition and products-per-customer to track progress toward the $560M profit scenario
